1800	Noach himself isn't the point; he is faulted so that it be explained to others
1801	that they should not learn
1802	from him in the future.
1803	So too at the end of the Torah, the Rebbe asks, which we read
1804	on Simchat Torah, Chatan Torah, that they wept for Moshe Rabbeinu
1805	thirty days, yet it doesn't say "all the House of Israel" as it does for Aharon.
1806	That is because Aharon pursued peace, he made peace between a man
1807	and his wife and so on, so all the House of Israel wept for him.
1808	How is it that, in the very portrayal of Moshe Rabbeinu, the peak of his ascent,
1809	something seems to come out as a lack, that Moshe Rabbeinu is less good than Aharon?
1810	It's the very same question.
1811	How can it be, when you are actually praising someone,
1812	that things come out that aren't the very best, a hundred percent?
1813	It means that this is what Moshe himself dictated: he wants it written, so that they not learn that he is the type
1814	who truly has no time or ability to make peace
1815	between people.
1816	He wants future generations to rule the halachah that on this particular point
1817	they should not learn from me.
1818	On this point, learn from Aharon. The same goes for Noach.
1819	Rabbi Yitzchak, who says it is a fault
1820	that he did not pray for his generation; and once you justify it, they also say he couldn't
1821	invoke the merit of the fathers, he had no merit of the fathers with which to pray for them, fine, so
1822	in that context he truly had no way to pray for his generation.
1823	But so that in our generation we do not learn from him, not to pray for the generation, not to identify with the generation, not to make any
1824	effort, it is forbidden to learn from him.
1825	Therefore one who rules halachah, it is like what is written, that the Torah added eight letters so as not to utter a derogatory word.
1826	But what is written?
1827	That this is only a narrative.
1828	If it touches on halachah, then we say "impure."
1829	Anything that touches on the law, we must say the word "impure," not say "not pure."
1830	If it is a story, then don't let the word "impure" leave your mouth.
1831	But if it is halachah, you must say that it is impure.
1832	That is from this side, for the sake of learning the law.
1833	Now, one who uses many, many more
1834	letters so as not to bring out a derogatory word from his mouth, that too comes from his
1835	right brain,
1836	the side of chesed.
1837	That is roughly it.
1838	But someone from the left side who has to rule halachah because it touches others,
1839	it is not a story about that individual.
1840	This also touches very much on journalism.
1841	However forbidden it is to tell derogatory stories about people.
1842	But what then?
1843	Sometimes there is an exception: to prevent someone else from learning
1844	a bad deed from a certain person, then it is obligatory.
1845	And if it is obligatory, you must say it straight.
1846	This is another great principle, a very important talk of the Rebbe
1847	on Parashat
1848	Noach.
1849	Let us return to our subject.
1850	There is "Reish Hormanuta d'Malka," which is the will to bring the world into being,
1851	which is Or Makif.
1852	Or Makif is in complete simplicity, it has no division whatsoever, it has no
1853	existence either; how can we explain this further.
1854	Inner light is what is called "galif galif uvatei reila."
1855	"Galif galif uvatei reila" is the ten sefirot hidden in the Emanator.
1856	Now, there is an expression in this chapter, and since it is condensed,
1857	it is so beautiful and important to contemplate that, even though it is only in passing, we will stop on it.
1858	He says that the ten sefirot hidden in the Emanator
1859	are in pshitut, in hitachdut and in hitarvut.
1860	So he writes.
1861	Pshitut...
1862	These are the ten sefirot hidden in the Emanator before the first tzimtzum, the root of the inner light.
1863	What is inner light?
1864	It is a light that is already hypothesized to illuminate
1865	the worlds with measure and limit.
1866	But for now, before the first tzimtzum, it has no measure or limit at all.
1867	And not only does it have no measure or limit, it is in pshitut and in all the sefirot.
1868	There are ten sefirot there.
1869	So everything is in pshitut, everything in hitachdut, and everything in hitarvut.
1870	Now, the moment I say the word hitarvut,
1871	it reminds me of what we learned a week ago about arevut, which is
1872	also guarantee among Jews, that all Israel are responsible one for the other, and guarantors
1873	for one another.
1874	So apparently the root of the arevut among souls also comes from a very
1875	high level before the tzimtzum, from the ten sefirot hidden in the Emanator, where all
1876	the sefirot are in complete union.
1877	From this comes, after the tzimtzum, that all Israel are responsible for one another.
1878	Now, that there is a level of hitachdut there, seemingly this is a descent.
1879	If he says here three words, one after the other, pshitut, hitachdut, hitarvut, then
1880	apparently these are three levels from top to bottom.
1881	So there is something higher than hitarvut, called hitachdut.
1882	So how does this also appear with us, Israel, after the tzimtzum?
1883	That we are one, "one nation on earth."
1884	All of us united, achdut.
1885	Let us go back up to the main point of the previous talk, that the main challenge
1886	of the movement is somehow a bit against the nature of the movement, in any
1887	case, to preserve unity.
1888	Even though there is here an inclination
1889	toward division because of the movement, to preserve
1890	unity.
1891	How can that be?
1892	It is a paradox.
1893	Apparently it can be because the true root, as explained in Chassidut regarding the four
1894	species, is that all their division, we also spoke about Israel, is only external.
1895	But inwardly they are all one.
1896	So it is with us, Israel.
1897	And with all the division we have...
1898	It is mainly expressed in the spine of the lulav, that we are one from the aspect of inwardness.
1899	That is hitachdut.
1900	Now there is something even higher than that, which is pshitut.
1901	Now, the pshitut of the ten sefirot hidden in the Emanator is not
1902	like the pshitut of the Or Makif.
1903	Because this pshitut, as he explains in the maamar, is a pshitut that is not meant to illuminate
1904	within limit, within existence.
1905	Whereas the pshitut of the ten sefirot hidden in the Emanator is meant, in the end, to illuminate
1906	within limit.
1907	So we must say that pshitut itself has two levels; afterwards he says something more.
1908	That even the light after the tzimtzum, before it enters the vessel, the light in itself is also
1909	pshitut.
1910	Therefore he says that the difference, the gap between
1911	the light before the tzimtzum and the light after the tzimtzum, is much, as if infinitely less
1912	than the difference between the vessels as they are hypothesized before the tzimtzum
1913	and the real vessels after the tzimtzum, which is totally
1914	incomparable.
1915	Before the tzimtzum they have no existence, and after the tzimtzum they are the existence.
1916	As if the light before the tzimtzum is in pshitut, and also after the tzimtzum
1917	it is in pshitut.
1918	In any case, these are three levels of pshitut.
1919	There is the pshitut of the Or Makif, and we need to understand what this word pshitut means.
